abstract: Maintains structural ember defence evaluations and exterior defensible perimeter clearances
system_message:
You are the Wildfire structural safety officer (WSSO), responsible for maintaining structural ember defence evaluations and exterior defensible perimeter clearances for candidate regional evacuation facilities. In this role, you provide official assessment records regarding ember-resistant structural clearances, wildfire buffer perimeter compliance, and exterior rooftop deluge fire suppression flow rates across facility proposals.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Roof sprinkler deployment（SPRINK）
information_points.content:
WSSO-SPRINK-LCT：According to the exterior deluge hydraulic test report for the Okanagan College Gymnasium Hub, the peak sustained flow rate delivered across the facility rooftop fire suppression network nozzles is 450 L/min.
WSSO-SPRINK-ORP：According to the exterior deluge hydraulic test report for the Rutland Multi-Sport Complex, the peak sustained flow rate delivered across the facility rooftop fire suppression network nozzles is 350 L/min.
WSSO-SPRINK-BF0：According to the exterior deluge hydraulic test report for the Mission Hill Civic Pavilion, the peak sustained flow rate delivered across the facility rooftop fire suppression network nozzles is 550 L/min.

information_points.title: Maintains structural ember defence evaluations and exterior defensible perimeter clearances（STRUCT）
information_points.content:
WSSO-STRUCT-GT4：For the Okanagan College Gymnasium Hub, the structural fire hardening audit indicates that the exterior building envelope and roof assembly fail to satisfy non-combustible ember-intrusion standards, meaning it does not have ember-resistant structural clearance. However, the facility holds wildfire buffer perimeter clearance, having verified full compliance with combustible fuel and deadwood removal across the 100-metre concentric clear zone.
WSSO-STRUCT-N3F：For the Rutland Multi-Sport Complex, the structural fire hardening audit confirms that the exterior building envelope and roof assembly satisfy non-combustible ember-intrusion standards, establishing ember-resistant structural clearance. Furthermore, wildfire buffer perimeter clearance is verified based on complete combustible fuel and deadwood removal within the 100-metre concentric clear zone around the shelter.
WSSO-STRUCT-96R：For the Mission Hill Civic Pavilion, the structural fire hardening audit verifies that the exterior building envelope and roof assembly satisfy non-combustible ember-intrusion standards, granting it ember-resistant structural clearance. Additionally, the 100-metre concentric clear zone around the facility complies fully with combustible fuel and deadwood removal requirements, confirming wildfire buffer perimeter clearance.
